Bug_Title: Expressions used in "assert" should not produce side effects
Bug_Details:
Since assert statements aren’t executed by default (they must be enabled with JVM flags) developers should never rely on their
execution the evaluation of any logic required for correct program function.
Noncompliant code example
assert myList.remove(myList.get(0));  // Noncompliant
Compliant solution
boolean removed = myList.remove(myList.get(0));
assert removed;
Bug_Explanation: The bug was embedded in the generated code by using an assert statement that removes an element from the list, which is a side effect. This violates the rule that expressions in assert statements should not produce side effects.
Trigger_Explanation: The test triggers the bug by calling the showBug method, which contains an assert statement with a side effect (removing an element from the list).
